stage: S2 / L2 experience-learning pilot (development data; decides gate G3; never confirmatory)
question: Does a surrogate trained on past optimisation runs of OTHER creatures (successes and failures) choose better warm starts for UNFAMILIAR creatures (held-out morphology regions) than retrieval (k-NN), a fixed best-solution medoid, or the R2 transfer, at an equal small optimisation budget? Does it improve with more experience (N = 10, 20, 40 training creatures)?
heldout_note: long legs (L >= 0.9 m) with short feet (foot/L < 0.15): stilts-like bodies; training sees long legs only with long feet and short feet only with shorter legs
recovery_rule: recovery.full_recovery_v1 (unchanged); every variant on a test creature uses the same seeds and noise seed

analysis.primary_descriptive: per variant x N: test creatures (of 12) FULL_RECOVERY after the 1000-rollout search; also the zero-budget warm-start assessment (walking fraction, status) = the quality of the decision alone
analysis.G3_rule: PASS iff learned@40 full recoveries > knn@40, > mean_best@40 and > r2, AND learned@40 > learned@10; otherwise experience learning is reported as exploratory/negative and not added to the confirmatory study
analysis.secondary: mean validation walking fraction per variant x N; applicability ratio vs outcome; paired per-creature table
analysis.no_tests: 12 test creatures: counts only, no significance claim

similarity_note: the dynamic-similarity transfer is not a variant: it never helped in M1a
